Job.JobTitle: Catastrophe Inside Adjuster - National General - National General
Job.JobDescription:
National General is a part of The Allstate Corporation, which means we have the same innovative drive that keeps us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. We offer home, auto and accident and health insurance, as well as other specialty niche insurance products, through a large network of independent insurance agents, as well as directly to consumers.

Job Description

Schedule, Travel & Hiring Locations

  • Work Arrangement: Fully remote; open to any U.S. time zone (excluding CA, AK, HI, WA, and PR).
  • Schedule: 5/2 model Monday through Friday, with flexibility between 7AM7PM CT. Must be able to adjust as needed, including occasional weekends, based on volume and event activity.
  • Travel: Occasional travel, up to 10%.

This job is responsible for investigating, negotiating, and settling moderately complex and occasionally complex claims involving the contents of a homeowner loss such as fire, water, or theft. The individual handles claims that typically require alternative housing during the restoration of the property. The individual handles claims virtually by leveraging technology tools and virtual resources to conduct a thorough analysis and evaluates damages, determines loss coverage, and authorizes payments.

A day in the life of an Catastrophe Inside Adjuster:

  • Spend your day handling claims virtually from home.
  • Handle escalated, complex claims involving contents, structure supplements, and/or additional living expense (ALE) damages.
  • Conduct thorough coverage investigations to ensure correct policy application.
  • Collaborate virtually with onsite vendors via advanced video technology to assess damages and prepare contents estimates.
  • Provide empathetic, customer-focused communication throughout the claims process.
  • Negotiate settlements in accordance with company standards.
  • Coordinate with structure adjusters for comprehensive claim handling.
  • Use data and analytics to support decision-making.
  • This role involves taking care of customers in their times of need. As a result, you must be willing to work some weekend and extended hours if necessary.

Training & Licensing

Training:

  • All licensing costs covered.
  • One month of fully paid training plus up to an additional month of on-the-job training.
  • Ongoing training opportunities for career growth.
  • If offered the role, you will go through virtual training. You will receive ongoing support, mentoring and coaching as you develop your career.

Notice of Licensing Requirement:

  • As a condition of employment, your office/area may require you to obtain an adjuster and/or an appraiser license, which includes passing an additional background check with the Department of Labor.
  • If applicable, you will be required to secure license(s) within 60 days of hire.
  • If required, the Hiring Manager will work with you, along with the Centralized Licensing team, to ensure you are properly licensed.

Youre a great match for this role if you:

  • Have a High School Diploma/GED (Bachelors degree preferred).
  • Bring 5+ years of property insurance claims handling experience.
  • Possess 2+ years of experience specifically related to Fire, Water, and Theft claims for Contents and Additional Living Expenses (ALE).
  • Have strong knowledge of all dwelling coverages, including UPP and ALE, with the ability to handle end-to-end claim processeswriting estimates, managing supplements, and finalizing claims.
  • Are familiar with working alongside Pilot adjusters and understand their workflow.
  • Have experience using Xactimate or similar estimating software for complex contents estimating.
  • Can work Central Standard Time hours.
  • Thrive in a fast-paced claims environment and are adaptable, organized, and detail-oriented.
  • Demonstrate strong customer service skills with excellent written and verbal communication.
  • Are able to work independently from a home environment.
  • Have bilingual skills and/or prior military experience (a plus).
  • Ideally possess comprehensive knowledge across all coverages.

Sign-On Bonus

Eligible for a $1,000 Licensing Sign-On Bonus if you possess applicable active licenses (e.g., Home Resident Property & Casualty License, DHS Florida or Texas License, Appraiser License). Former Allstate employees seeking rehire are not eligible for this bonus.

Technology & Internet Requirements

  • Access to modem and internet connection required
  • Dedicated, distraction-free workspace in your home required
  • Remote employees are eligible for internet reimbursement (minimum speeds: 50 MBPS download / 5 MBPS upload)

Job.JobTitle: Account Executive Officer/Sr. Underwriter National Property
Job.CustomJobTypeName: Insurance Underwriter, Underwriting, Insurance Account Executive
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Pay: $123,400 to $203,600 a year
  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Centennial, CO
  • Benefits: Health insurance, 401(k), paid time off

Full job description

Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That's the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Compensation Overview

The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.

Salary Range

$123,400.00 - $203,600.00

Target Openings

1

What Is the Opportunity?

National Property provides tailored property protection solutions for high value, complex risks across a wide array of industries. The Account Executive Officer (AEO), National Property will partner with agents and brokers to provide coverage for new and renewal business based on customers' needs. This role is seen as a technical resource. As an AEO, you are decisive, detail-oriented, and know how to build relationships internally and externally to drive results. Your ability to independently assess complex risk and sell our products in challenging markets will contribute to the profitability and success of Travelers.

As of the date of this posting, Travelers anticipates that this posting will remain open until May 15, 2027.

What Will You Do?

  • Manage the profitability, growth, and retention of an assigned book of business.
  • Underwrite and skillfully negotiate complex customer accounts to minimize risk and maximize profitability. Additionally, occasionally negotiate and procure reinsurance to underwrite complex accounts.
  • May facilitate the placement of foreign admitted policies, serve as a resource to field Account Executives on global underwriting capabilities, as well as assist in the business development activities for such global underwriting services.
  • Cultivate and maintain relationships with internal partners within the business unit and across the enterprise to create sales plans and identify cross-selling opportunities.
  • Foster and maintain relationships with external partners by regularly meeting in person with agents and brokers to market and sell Travelers products with a goal of writing and retaining accounts consistent with our risk appetite. Must be able to travel to such meetings.
  • Identify and capture new business opportunities using consultative marketing and sales skills.
  • Independently develop and execute agency sales plans and frequently partner with your Managing Director (MD) to develop region/group sales plans.
  • May assist in the training and mentoring of less experienced Account Executives.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's degree.
  • Six to eight years of relevant underwriting experience with experience in National Property.
  • Deep knowledge of property-related products, the regulatory environment, and the local insurance market.
  • Deep financial acumen.
  • Strong critical thinking skills with the ability to proactively identify underwriting, marketing, or financial challenges and analyze available information to make timely decisions in alignment with our risk appetite.
  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to successfully negotiate in difficult situations with agents and brokers.
  • CPCU designation.

What is a Must Have?

  • Four years of underwriting, claim, operations, risk assessment, actuarial, sales, product, or finance experience.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members - including spouses, domestic partners, and children - are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

Employment Practices

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences. 

In accordance with local law, candidates seeking employment in Colorado are not required to disclose dates of attendance at or graduation from educational institutions.

If you are a candidate and have specific questions regarding the physical requirements of this role, please send us an email so we may assist you.

Travelers reserves the right to fill this position at a level above or below the level included in this posting.

To learn more about our comprehensive benefit programs please visit http://careers.travelers.com/life-at-travelers/benefits/.

Job.JobTitle: Auto Liability Claim Representative
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Pay: $68,700 to $113,400 a year
  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Hartford, CT
  • Education: High school diploma or GED
  • Benefits: Health insurance, 401(k), paid time off

Full job description

Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That's the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Compensation Overview

The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.

Salary Range

$68,700.00 - $113,400.00

Target Openings

1

What Is the Opportunity?

As a Claim Rep, Auto Liability, you will be responsible for managing and investigating low to moderate complexity injury and/or property damage claims including customer contact, determining coverage, evaluating liability, assessing damages, establishing timely reserves, and issue timely and accurate payments within appropriate authority and oversight. In this fast-paced, detail-oriented and customer-focused role, you will work closely with customers, claimants, attorneys, and other parties to ensure claims are resolved accurately and efficiently while maintaining a high level of professionalism, empathy, and service. You may provide training and coaching to less experienced claim professionals.

What Will You Do?

  • Manage an active caseload of injury and/or property damage claims from first notice of loss through resolution within level of authority. Typically, handles low to moderately complex personal and/or business insurance liability claims which may include coverage disputes and contractual indemnity issues.
  • Gather and thoroughly investigate information by contacting all relevant parties to determine coverage, evaluate liability exposure, assess bodily injury and/or property damage, and establish appropriate reserves in accordance with policy terms and management guidance. Leverage internal resources, as appropriate.
  • Provide timely and professional communication to customers, opposing counsel, third-party vendors, internal stakeholders, and other parties.
  • Negotiate with multiple constituents (e.g., claimants, attorneys, representatives) and convey claim settlements within authority and issue payments timely and accurately.
  • Handle low complexity litigation.
  • Maintain accurate records of claim activity in claim management systems.
  • Adapt to new technology implementations, system upgrades, and digital tool rollouts, particularly in the areas of AI while maintaining productivity and service quality.
  • Acquire and maintain relevant Insurance License(s) to comply with state and Travelers' requirements within three months of starting the job.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's Degree.
  • Two years of bodily injury claim experience.
  • Active adjuster license, where required by state law.
  • Experience with claims management systems, with advanced skills in Microsoft Office and enterprise technology systems and platforms.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to convey information clearly and professionally to multiple stakeholders.
  • Ability to analyze situations, exercise sound judgement, make effective decisions.
  • Exceptional customer service skills and commitment to providing a positive experience for customers; ability to manage difficult conversations with empathy and professionalism.
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills with the ability to manage a high-volume workload and prioritize effectively.
  • Proven conflict resolution and negotiation skills; ability to handle complex or disputed claims and negotiate settlements.
  • Ability to manage stress, navigate difficult situations, and maintain composure and professionalism under pressure while always taking accountability for decisions.
  • Strong understanding of insurance principles and terminology, with working knowledge of state insurance regulations, claim handling requirements, and fair claims practices.
  • Demonstrated ability comprehend and analyze policy language.
  • Ability to quickly learn from experience and apply it to new situations with speed and flexibility.

What is a Must Have?

  • High School Diploma or GED.
  • One year of bodily injury liability, property damage liability, or comparable claim related experience or successful completion of required Travelers Claim Representative training program.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members - including spouses, domestic partners, and children - are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

Employment Practices

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences. 

In accordance with local law, candidates seeking employment in Colorado are not required to disclose dates of attendance at or graduation from educational institutions.

If you are a candidate and have specific questions regarding the physical requirements of this role, please send us an email so we may assist you.

Travelers reserves the right to fill this position at a level above or below the level included in this posting.

To learn more about our comprehensive benefit programs please visit http://careers.travelers.com/life-at-travelers/benefits/.

If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

Employment Practices

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences. 

In accordance with local law, candidates seeking employment in Colorado are not required to disclose dates of attendance at or graduation from educational institutions.

If you are a candidate and have specific questions regarding the physical requirements of this role, please send us an email so we may assist you.

Travelers reserves the right to fill this position at a level above or below the level included in this posting.

To learn more about our comprehensive benefit programs please visit http://careers.travelers.com/life-at-travelers/benefits/.

Job.JobTitle: Associate Attorney - Special Investigation Unit and Liability
Job.JobDescription:
Description

This role is primarily remote in the state of New York except for required appearances.

At Liberty Mutual, were committed to delivering exceptional legal services to our customers around the world, working to uphold and protect our policyholders rights and positively impacting our business. As an Associate Attorney at Liberty Mutual, youll join a diverse team that values a healthy work/life balance and enjoy benefits that include eligible performance bonuses, 20 days of flexible time off each year, personal holidays, and a 401(k) plan with matching contributions. If youre looking for a place to build a long-term career while making a positive difference, consider joining our legal team in a role that combines special investigations legal support with liability litigation.

Liberty Mutual Insurance offers an engaging opportunity for an Associate Attorney whose practice will focus on special investigations matters and on liability litigation. Under moderate supervision, you will provide legal support for the investigation and evaluation of potentially fraudulent or materially misrepresented insurance claims, working collaboratively with Special Investigations Unit (SIU) professionals, claims representatives, and senior counsel. You will also represent Liberty Mutual and its policyholders, as appropriate, in moderately complex civil litigation involving claims for monetary damages arising from personal injury or property damage.

You will apply your legal knowledge, investigative judgment, research skills, and client relationship capabilities to develop facts, assess legal risks, and support fair, well-reasoned claim decisions and effective litigation outcomes in a collaborative and supportive environment.

Responsibilities:

Special Investigations

Investigative Legal Support: Partner with SIU professionals and claims representatives to develop legally sound investigation strategies for claims involving suspected fraud, material misrepresentation, or other potentially improper activity. Identify relevant legal issues, evidentiary needs, and appropriate next steps while maintaining an objective, fact-based approach.

Examinations and Evidence Development: Prepare for and conduct examinations under oath, where authorized and appropriate, and assist with witness interviews, document requests, and other fact-development activities. Evaluate testimony, claim documentation, and other evidence to identify inconsistencies and determine whether additional investigation is warranted.

Legal Research and Claim Evaluation: Research and analyze applicable law concerning insurance fraud, misrepresentation, policy conditions, and investigative procedures. Provide clear and reasoned legal opinions to support claim evaluation, coordinating with coverage counsel or other designated counsel when appropriate.

Investigation-Related Litigation: Handle or support litigation arising from special investigations within the scope of the assigned practice, including discovery, depositions, motions, hearings, and trial preparation. Collaborate with senior counsel on matters involving moderately complex investigative and evidentiary issues.

SIU Collaboration and Knowledge Sharing: Maintain effective working relationships with SIU, Claims, and legal partners. Share legal developments and practical guidance that strengthen investigative practices, evidence preservation, and documentation quality.

Liability Litigation

Litigation Execution: Manage assigned personal injury and property damage liability cases from inception through resolution, including pleadings, discovery, depositions, hearings, mediations, and trials. Support Senior Trial Counsel and Senior Litigation Counsel in case preparation, management, and trial execution.

Risk Evaluation and Case Resolution: Assess liability, damages, and litigation exposure. Develop defense strategies and collaborate with claims representatives, insured clients, and senior counsel to facilitate effective case resolutions.

Client Advisory and Relationship Management: Provide strategic legal advice and clear, consistent, and timely updates to insured clients and claims professionals. Maintain strong client relationships through transparent communication and alignment with case objectives.

Responsibilities Across Both Practice Areas

Technology Utilization: Use e-discovery, legal research, and case management technologies to improve efficiency and support effective collaboration with remote team members.

Documentation Accuracy and Compliance: Prepare accurate, thorough, and timely legal documents, investigative assessments, and case reports in accordance with applicable legal standards and client expectations.

Contribution to Organizational Improvement: Participate in initiatives that enhance efficiency, effectiveness, and best practices within Staff Legal and Global Legal & Compliance.

Ethical Compliance and Professional Judgment: Uphold the highest standards of legal ethics, confidentiality, and professional responsibility. Recognize and appropriately address conflicts of interest, preserve applicable privileges, and ensure investigative and litigation activities comply with governing law and licensing requirements.

Qualifications
  • Juris Doctor (JD) or LLB degree from an accredited law school.
  • Admission to the bar in NY and in good standing; special licenses to practice before particular boards or federal courts may be required.
  • General knowledge of insurance law
  • Proficient in e-discovery, case management systems, and basic legal analysis tools.
  • Strong analytical, research, and legal writing skills.
  • Basic knowledge of negotiation techniques including preparation, active listening, and problem-solving.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage cases from start to finish under supervision.
  • Effective communication and persuasion skills, both written and oral.
  • Ability to collaborate with clients, claims professionals, and senior attorneys.
  • Organized, process-oriented with strong time management skills.
About Us

Pay Philosophy: The typical starting salary range for this role is determined by a number of factors including skills, experience, education, certifications and location. The full salary range for this role reflects the competitive labor market value for all employees in these positions across the national market and provides an opportunity to progress as employees grow and develop within the role. Some roles at Liberty Mutual have a corresponding compensation plan which may include commission and/or bonus earnings at rates that vary based on multiple factors set forth in the compensation plan for the role.

At Liberty Mutual, our goal is to create a workplace where everyone feels valued, supported, and can thrive. We build an environment that welcomes a wide range of perspectives and experiences, with inclusion embedded in every aspect of our culture and reflected in everyday interactions. This comes to life through comprehensive benefits, workplace flexibility, professional development opportunities, and a host of opportunities provided through our Employee Resource Groups. Each employee plays a role in creating our inclusive culture, which supports every individual to do their best work. Together, we cultivate a community where everyone can make a meaningful impact for our business, our customers, and the communities we serve.

We value your hard work, integrity and commitment to make things better, and we put people first by offering you benefits that support your life and well-being. To learn more about our benefit offerings please visit: https://www.libertymutualgroup.com/about-lm/careers/benefits

Job.JobTitle: Senior Technical Claims Specialist, Construction Complex
Job.JobDescription:
Description

Liberty Mutuals Specialized Claims group has an immediate opening on our Complex Construction Claims Team. Were seeking an experienced claims professional who thrives on challenging, high-exposure commercial casualty matters arising from construction operations including complex Commercial General Liability (CGL) and Construction Injury/Liability claims (all litigated or high-exposure losses $500,000+). You will own matters end-to-end, managing coverage and liability strategy, directing investigations and experts, coordinating litigation and outside counsel, and driving timely, defensible resolutions for our Construction Industry accounts. (Note: this role does not handle construction defect claims.)

Why this role is a great fit for you

  • Work exclusively on technically complex, high-exposure construction-related casualty claims that require advanced legal and claims judgment.
  • Autonomy to set strategy, reserves and resolution plans, with authority to direct investigations and manage outside counsel and experts.
  • Opportunity to influence outcomes across underwriting, product and legal teams and to be a recognized technical resource on construction liability issues.
  • Exposure to multi-party, catastrophic injury and cross-coverage matters valuable experience for senior claims leaders and litigators.
  • Flexibility with structure. This role is primarily remote, with a light-touch office cadence - just two in-office days per month for those who live within 50 miles of one of our hub locations in Boston, MA; Hoffman Estates, IL; Indianapolis, IN; Lake Oswego, OR; Las Vegas, NV; Plano, TX; Suwanee, GA; Chandler, AZ; and Weatogue, CT. Policy is subject to change.

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage a caseload of complex, litigated construction-related losses ($500K+) from assignment through resolution: coverage analysis, liability assessment, investigation planning, reserving, negotiation, settlement or denial where appropriate.
  • Lead coverage interpretation and application for issues commonly encountered in construction claims: additional insureds, tenders, indemnity agreements, other insurance, SIR/deductible mechanics, primary vs. excess placement, and limits erosion.
  • Direct litigation strategy: analyze pleadings, manage discovery and depositions, evaluate venue and trial risk, prepare for mediations and settlement conferences, and recommend and implement resolution strategies.
  • Build and lead the working team for each matter: coordinate Home-Office Legal, defense counsel, SIU when appropriate, medical and causation experts, accident reconstructionist, engineers, and other technical consultants.
  • Select, supervise and evaluate outside counsel, including establishing budgets, staffing plans, billing guidelines expectations, and performance measures.
  • Set and adjust reserves based on defensible analysis and develop settlement strategies that protect the companys interests while advancing timely resolution.
  • Maintain accurate, complete file documentation and ensure secure handling of financial transactions and claim information.
  • Collaborate proactively with Underwriting, Risk Control, Reinsurance/Excess, Product and Subrogation teams; identify and communicate trends and technical insights.
  • Mentor and coach less-experienced claims professionals and contribute to team training, process improvements, and special projects.

What we seek in a candidate?

An experienced claims professional with a strong Commercial General Liability and/or Construction Liability background (preferably with claims $500,000 and above), sound judgment on complex coverage and liability questions, and the confidence to lead files, mentor others, and manage litigation strategy independently.

Qualifications

What were looking for Required

    • Substantial hands-on experience handling complex, litigated Commercial General Liability and/or Construction Liability claims at high exposure levels (preferably $500,000+).
    • Deep working knowledge of CGL and Construction Liability coverages and typical construction-related policy issues (additional insured wording, contractual indemnity, other insurance, primary/excess interaction, SIRs/deductibles).
    • Proven litigation management experience: selecting/managing defense counsel, directing discovery strategy, preparing for mediation/trial, evaluating exposure and settlement leverage.
    • Strong technical judgment and the ability to articulate and defend coverage and liability positions to legal, underwriting, and management partners.
    • Track record of using and directing experts (medical, causation, engineers, reconstruction) on complex causation and damages issues.
    • Excellent negotiation, communication and stakeholder management skills.
    • Ability to manage multiple high-priority matters and meet deadlines under pressure.
    • Bachelors degree (preferred) and relevant claims/insurance industry certifications or licenses as applicable.
    • Ability to obtain and maintain needed All-lines Adjuster license. Claims/Industry certifications a plus!
About Us

Job.JobTitle: Senior Underwriter / Account Executive Officer - Commercial Accounts / Middle Market Underwriter
Job.CustomJobTypeName: Commercial Lines Underwriter, Underwriting, Insurance Underwriter
Job.JobDescription:
Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That's the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Compensation Overview

The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.

Salary Range

$112,000.00 - $184,800.00

Target Openings

1

What Is the Opportunity?

Commercial Accounts offers a wide array of guaranteed-cost products to mid-size businesses. Total account solutions include General Liability, Property, Automobile, Workers' Compensation, and Lead Umbrella. The Account Executive Officer (AEO), Commercial Accounts will partner with agents and brokers to provide property, general liability, commercial auto, and/or workers' compensation coverage for new and renewal business based on customers' needs. This role is seen as a technical resource. As an AEO, you are decisive, detail-oriented, and know how to build relationships internally and externally to drive results. Your ability to independently assess complex risk and sell our products in challenging markets will contribute to the profitability and success of Travelers.

What Will You Do?

  • Manage the profitability, growth, and retention of an assigned book of business.
  • Underwrite and skillfully negotiate complex customer accounts to minimize risk and maximize profitability.
  • Cultivate and maintain relationships with internal partners within the business unit and across the enterprise to create sales plans and identify cross-selling opportunities.
  • Foster and maintain relationships with external partners by regularly meeting in person with agents and brokers to market and sell Travelers products with a goal of writing and retaining accounts consistent with our risk appetite. Must be able to travel to such meetings.
  • Identify and capture new business opportunities using consultative marketing and sales skills.
  • Independently develop and execute agency sales plans and frequently partner with your Managing Director (MD) to develop region/group sales plans.
  • May assist in the training and mentoring of less experienced Account Executives.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's degree.
  • Six to eight years of relevant underwriting experience with experience in commercial lines.
  • Deep knowledge of commercial lines products, the regulatory environment, and the local insurance market.
  • Strong critical thinking skills with the ability to proactively identify underwriting, marketing, or financial challenges and analyze available information to make timely decisions in alignment with our risk appetite.
  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to successfully negotiate in difficult situations with agents and brokers.
  • CPCU designation.

What is a Must Have?

  • Four years of underwriting, claim, operations, risk assessment, actuarial, sales, product, or finance experience.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members - including spouses, domestic partners, and children - are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

Employment Practices

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences. 

In accordance with local law, candidates seeking employment in Colorado are not required to disclose dates of attendance at or graduation from educational institutions.

If you are a candidate and have specific questions regarding the physical requirements of this role, please send us an email so we may assist you.

Travelers reserves the right to fill this position at a level above or below the level included in this posting.

To learn more about our comprehensive benefit programs please visit http://careers.travelers.com/life-at-travelers/benefits/.

This position services Insureds/Agents in and around Prescott, AZ. The selected candidate must reside in or be willing to relocate at their own expense to the assigned territory.

As an Associate Claim Rep, Outside Property, you will receive comprehensive training in claim handling, customer service, and policy interpretation while working alongside experienced claim professionals. This position focuses on developing your skills and knowledge to successfully manage 1st party property claims.

This program is typically 9-12 months and upon successful completion of this program you will have the skills needed to handle claims independently and progress toward full claims handling responsibility.

This position is based remotely with work at residential and commercial locations with a combination of mobile work, work from your primary residence, or the nearest Travelers office.

What Will You Do?

  • Actively participate in structured training classes covering insurance policies, specific claim processes, systems, and procedures, including virtual, classroom, and on-the-job training.
  • Review, investigate, and document 1st party property claims under direct supervision.
  • Gather information from policyholders, claimants, witnesses, and third-party providers.
  • Learn to investigate and evaluate all relevant facts and information (including but not limited to analyzing leases, contracts, by-laws and other relevant documents which may have an impact). Determine and apply coverage for building damages per policy terms.
  • Establish accurate scope of damages for building and contents losses and utilizes as a basis for written estimates and/or computer assisted estimates.
  • Provide timely and professional communication to customers, claimants, and internal stakeholders.
  • Maintain accurate records of claim activity in claim management systems.
  • Demonstrate openness to continuous learning, particularly in AI and digital transformation.
  • Adapt to new technology implementations, system upgrades, and digital tool rollouts while maintaining productivity and service quality.
  • Acquire and maintain relevant Insurance License(s) and/or a UAS Remote Pilot Certification to comply with federal, state, and Travelers requirements within three months of starting the job.
  • Assess and inspect all areas of a dwelling or structure, including roofs, attics, crawl spaces, and other confined areas. Ability to carry, set up, and climb ladders weighing approximately 38-49 pounds.
  • May require extensive travel, including overnight stays, to support customers across multiple locations.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's Degree.
  • Previous internship or work experience in customer service or insurance.
  • Willingness to obtain an active adjuster license where required by state law.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook); willingness to learn claims management and estimating software.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to convey information clearly and professionally.
  • Ability to exercise sound judgement and make effective decisions within established authority.
  • Exceptional customer service skills and commitment to providing a positive experience for insureds and claimants.
  • Attention to detail and organizational skills; ability to manage multiple tasks and prioritize effectively.
  • Basic conflict resolution skills; willingness to learn techniques for facilitating productive discussions and negotiations.
  • Demonstrate openness to continuous learning.

What is a Must Have?

  • High School Diploma or GED and one year of customer service experience.
  • Valid driver's license.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members - including spouses, domestic partners, and children - are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.

What Is the Opportunity?

As a Sr Technical Specialist, General Liability, you will be responsible for managing and investigating complex and higher-severity injury and/or property damage claims including customer contact, determining coverage, evaluating liability, assessing damages, establishing timely reserves, and issue timely and accurate payments within appropriate authority and oversight. In this senior technical role, you will leverage advanced expertise in claims management, investigative techniques, coverage evaluation, and settlement negotiation to ensure timely and fair resolution. You will foster positive, professional relationships with customers and key stakeholders on matters involving significant litigation and extended resolution timelines. You will actively mentor and coach Claim Professionals, including providing higher-severity claims mentoring to enhance higher-level skill sets.

What Will You Do?

  • Independently manage an active caseload of injury and/or property damage claims and litigation from first notice of loss through resolution within level of authority. Typically, handles personal and/or business insurance high complexity liability claims with coverage disputes and contractual indemnity issues.
  • Gather and thoroughly investigate information by contacting all relevant parties to determine coverage, evaluate liability exposure, assess bodily injury and/or property damage which may include personal and advertising injury claims, and establish appropriate reserves in accordance with policy terms and management guidance.
  • Provide timely and professional communication to customers, representatives, opposing counsel, third-party vendors, and internal stakeholders.
  • Develop and execute advanced resolution strategies and coordinate internal and external resources to conduct comprehensive claim investigations and evaluations.
  • Partner with Counsel to develop, direct, and execute litigation management strategies.
  • Manage multi-party negotiations with key stakeholders to achieve optimal claim resolutions within delegated authority limits.
  • Maintain accurate records of claim activity in claim management systems.

Job.JobTitle: Associate Claim Rep Auto Express
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Pay: $40,200 to $66,200 a year
  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Hartford, CT
  • Education: High school diploma or GED
  • Benefits: Health insurance, 401(k), paid time off

Full job description

Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That's the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Compensation Overview

The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.

Salary Range

$40,200.00 - $66,200.00

Target Openings

5

What Is the Opportunity?

As an Associate Claim Rep, Auto Express, you will receive comprehensive training in claim handling, customer service, and policy interpretation while working alongside experienced claim professionals. This position focuses on developing your skills and knowledge to successfully manage personal insurance claims involving various types of automobiles and property damage. This role involves frequent customer interactions through telephone and written communications. This program is typically 8-12 months and upon successful completion of this program, you will have the skills needed to handle claims independently and progress toward full claims handling responsibility.

What Will You Do?

  • Actively participate in structured training classes covering insurance policies, specific claim processes, systems, and procedures, including virtual, classroom, and on-the-job training.
  • Assess coverage to determine compensability.
  • Investigate by gathering information from policyholders and claimants to verify the facts of loss.
  • Assess coverage and bring claim to resolution with accurate payment in a timely manner.
  • Communicate and apprise all parties regarding claim status.
  • Maintain accurate records of claim activity in claim management systems.
  • Adapt to new technology implementations, system upgrades, and digital tool rollouts, particularly in the areas of AI while maintaining productivity and service quality.
  • Acquire and maintain relevant Insurance License(s) to comply with state and Travelers' requirements within three months of starting the job.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's Degree.
  • Previous internship or work experience in customer service or insurance.
  • Willingness to obtain an active adjuster license where required by state law.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook); willingness to learn claims management systems.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to convey information clearly and professionally.
  • Ability to exercise sound judgement and make effective decisions within established authority.
  • Exceptional customer service skills and commitment to providing a positive experience for insureds and claimants.
  • Attention to detail and organizational skills; ability to manage multiple tasks and prioritize effectively.
  • Basic conflict resolution skills; willingness to learn techniques for facilitating productive discussions and negotiations.
  • Demonstrate openness to continuous learning.

What is a Must Have?

  • High School Diploma or GED and one year of customer service experience.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members - including spouses, domestic partners, and children - are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

Employment Practices

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences. 

In accordance with local law, candidates seeking employment in Colorado are not required to disclose dates of attendance at or graduation from educational institutions.

If you are a candidate and have specific questions regarding the physical requirements of this role, please send us an email so we may assist you.

Travelers reserves the right to fill this position at a level above or below the level included in this posting.

To learn more about our comprehensive benefit programs please visit http://careers.travelers.com/life-at-travelers/benefits/.

Job.JobTitle: Director, Global Trade Compliance
Job.JobDescription:
Overview of Position


Reporting to the AVP, Connected Living Compliance, this position is responsible for leading Assurant's global trade compliance program and ensuring compliance with all applicable import, export, sanctions, and customs regulations. In addition to enterprise related trade activities, this role actively supports the movement of mobile devices, device components, service parts, accessories, and related technologies across global markets while enabling efficient customer, carrier, OEM, repair, refurbishment, and logistics operations.


The Director serves as a strategic advisor to Connected Living leadership and business stakeholders, balancing compliance obligations with customer commitments, operational efficiency, and commercial objectives.


This role will also partner, coordinate, and align global trade compliance activities and strategies with the Director, Global Supply Chain Compliance.


What will my duties and responsibilities be in this job?


Global Trade Compliance Leadership (45%)


  • Develop, implement, and continuously improve Assurant's global trade compliance program.
  • Establish governance, policies, procedures, and internal controls covering import, export, sanctions, and customs compliance.
  • Ensure compliance with:
    • U.S. Export Administration Regulations (EAR)
    • OFAC sanctions requirements
    • U.S. Customs regulations
    • International customs laws and regulations
    • Foreign trade regulations in countries where Assurant operates
  • Provide strategic guidance to executive leadership on global trade risks and opportunities.
  • Identify and implement value-creation opportunities, including duty drawback, free trade agreements, foreign trade zones, tariff engineering, and other lawful duty mitigation strategies.

Import Compliance and Customs Management (20%)


  • Oversee global customs compliance for mobile devices, service parts, accessories, and technology.
  • Ensure accurate:
    • HTS classifications
    • Country-of-origin determinations
    • Customs valuation
    • Duty assessment
  • Manage customs brokers and trade service providers.
    • Identify and implement duty savings strategies and opportunities.
  • Support optimization of global supply chain costs and customs efficiency.

Export Controls and Sanctions Compliance (20%)


  • Oversee export classification activities for devices, components, software, and technology.
  • Ensure compliance with export controls.
  • Lead restricted-party screening and sanctions compliance programs.
  • Provide guidance regarding cross-border shipments, technology transfers, and international business transactions.
  • Manage export licensing requirements and government authorizations when required.
  • Drive global alignment for HTS classification, country of origin, customs valuation, and Export Control Classification Number (ECCN) determinations.
  • Maintain awareness of export-controlled technology, software, encryption, and restricted-access information requirements applicable to Assurant operations.
  • Assess and manage export control risks involving restricted destinations, restricted parties, military end users, military end uses, and controlled technologies, software, or technical data; develop procedures for end-use/end-user due diligence, escalation, licensing analysis, and transaction holds where required.

Risk Management and Compliance Governance (10%)


  • Conduct enterprise-wide trade compliance risk assessments.
  • Develop and maintain trade compliance controls and monitoring programs.
  • Lead internal audits and compliance reviews.
  • Establish compliance metrics, dashboards, and executive reporting.
  • Investigate compliance incidents and manage corrective actions.
  • Lead government audits, inquiries, disclosures, and remediation activities.
  • Assists in remediating trade compliance issues as necessary, including but not limited to putting together project plans, connecting resources to find solutions, documenting resolutions, and documenting remediation plans.
  • Supports internal compliance audits and assists with managing external audits or inquiries from government agencies Maintains accurate data and recordkeeping to include collecting and retaining records in response to third-party inquiries relating to Assurant compliance practices and business activities.

Training and Culture (5%)


  • Develop and deliver trade compliance training and awareness programs.
  • Ensure employees understand their responsibilities related to international trade activities.
  • Maintain training records and support audit readiness.

Number of Direct Reports


  • 1-2 including a Compliance Analyst

Financial Responsibility


  • Signoff on responsible expenses, input on annual budget.

What are the requirements needed for this position?


Experience


  • Minimum of 8 years of progressive experience in global trade compliance.
  • At least 5 years of leadership experience.
  • Experience supporting multinational import/export operations.
  • Experience managing customs and export compliance programs.
  • Experience supporting technology, telecommunications, consumer electronics, mobile device, repair/refurbishment, or logistics industries preferred.

Education & Certifications


  • Bachelors' degree required, Master's or JD preferred

Preferred Certifications


  • Licensed Customs Broker (LCB)
  • Certified Export Specialist (CES)
  • Certified Customs Specialist (CCS)
  • Certified U.S. Export Compliance Officer (CUSECO)

Preferred Technical Expertise


  • EAR
  • OFAC sanctions compliance
  • Customs valuation
  • HTS classification
  • Country-of-origin analysis
  • Free Trade Agreements
  • Duty drawback
  • Foreign Trade Zones (FTZ)
  • Reverse logistics operations
  • Mobile device repair and refurbishment supply chains

Leadership Competencies

The candidate will be able to provide examples of successfully demonstrating the following leadership competencies:


  • Internal client-orientation with a constructive approach to resolution of issues. A style which builds alliances within the organization.
  • Ability to establish credibility with business owners, including senior and executive leadership, and influence through professional communication, work product, etc.
  • Solutions-oriented, demonstrated growth mindset.
  • Proven ability to build and maintain effective cross-functional relationships with clients, colleagues and stakeholders of various levels and areas throughout the organization.
  • Ability to lead change efforts through effective communication and persuasion.
  • Creative, resilient, and flexible style and approach to handling complex issues with high tolerance for ambiguity
  • Demonstrated leadership experience on leveraging data to drive actionable insights for risk or compliance programs
  • Clear written, visual and verbal communication skills, including ability to adjust messages dependent on audiences ranging from front-line employees to executive
  • Cultural competency and executive-level presence to work with the business and regional leadership teams around the world
  • Strong analytical, organizational, problem-solving, and follow-up skills. Ability to interpret rules and guidelines, and then conceptualize and implement into policies, procedures, and controls.
  • Excellent and demonstrated project management skills, and attention to detail in leading projects and activities in a global organization. Ability to prioritize and simultaneously execute on multiple projects and ability to organize and analyze complex information and data
  • Sound and independent judgment, and demonstrated prudence and maturity
  • Commitment to driving a culture of ethics and integrity
  • Cultivate a high-performing trade compliance team through coaching, mentoring, accountability, and development of trade compliance professionals.

Skills


The candidate will be able to demonstrate proficiency in the following skills:


  • Proficiency in the Microsoft Office Suite with specific emphasis in Word, Excel, PowerPoint
  • The ability to work in a fast-paced environment with several simultaneous deliverables
  • Program of project management skills

What other skills/experience would be helpful to have?


  • Experience in mobile or technology industries
  • Ability to use AI tools such as Copilot, ChatGPT, etc
  • Supply chain and vendor risk management experience

#AssurantProudMS


Pay Range

$122,400.00 - $204,400.00

If no application deadline is provided, this role may be a pipeline requisition, and we'll continue to collect applications on an ongoing basis, or there is no requirement for this information in the location where the role is posted.

Any posted pay range considers a wide range of compensation factors, including candidate background, experience, and work location, while also allowing for salary growth within the position.

Helping People Thrive in a Connected World

What's the culture like at Assurant?
Our unique culture is a big reason why talented people choose Assurant. Named a Best/Great Place to Work in 14 countries and awarded the Fortune America's Most Innovative Companies recognition, we bring together top talent around the world. Although we have a wide variety of skills and experiences, we share common characteristics that are uniquely Assurant. A passion for service. An ability to innovate in practical ways. And a willingness to take chances. We call our culture The Assurant Way.

Company Overview
Assurant is a leading global business services company that supports, protects, and connects major consumer purchases. A Fortune 500 company with a presence in 21 countries, Assurant supports the advancement of the connected world by partnering with the world's leading brands to develop innovative solutions and deliver an enhanced customer experience through mobile device solutions, extended service contracts, vehicle protection services, renters insurance, lender-placed insurance products, and other specialty products.

Job.JobTitle: Senior Manager, TPA Claims Strategy & Governance
Job.JobDescription:
The Opportunity


We are looking for an experienced claims leader to lead the strategy, governance, and performance of our third-party administrator (TPA) claim programs across multiple products, business segments, and jurisdictions.

This is a highly visible leadership role with responsibility for ensuring our TPA partners deliver fair, timely, accurate, and compliant claim outcomes while meeting our expectations for customer experience, financial performance, and operational quality.


You will serve as the senior business owner for key TPA relationships, lead a team of claims and vendor oversight professionals, partner closely with senior leaders across the organization, and influence how we manage outsourced claims operations at an enterprise level.


This role is ideal for a strategic P&C claims leader who knows how to balance technical claims expertise, vendor accountability, financial discipline, and strong relationships to drive results.


What You'll Do


Lead TPA strategy and governance

  • Set the strategy, operating model, and governance framework for TPA claim programs across products, programs, jurisdictions, and business segments.
  • Establish and continuously improve service-level agreements, performance scorecards, claim-handling guidelines, authority levels, escalation protocols, and reporting standards.
  • Lead TPA selection, onboarding, implementation, renewal, transition, and termination activities while protecting claim continuity and customer service.

Own TPA performance and relationships

  • Serve as the senior relationship owner with TPA leadership, leading business reviews, performance discussions, escalations, and negotiations.
  • Hold partners accountable for claim inventories, cycle time, customer experience, claim quality, reserve adequacy, settlement accuracy, leakage, litigation activity, regulatory compliance, and contractual commitments.
  • Assess TPA capacity, staffing, training, licensing, business continuity, data security, and catastrophe readiness, and drive action plans when risks emerge.

Provide senior claims leadership

  • Provide strategic direction on complex, high-exposure, litigated, escalated, or disputed claims, including coverage, reserves, litigation strategy, and settlement approach within delegated authority.
  • Lead the audit, calibration, and quality assurance framework for TPA claim handling.
  • Identify performance trends and root causes and ensure corrective actions deliver sustainable improvement.

Lead and develop a high-performing team

  • Lead, coach, and develop managers, claim consultants, relationship managers, and vendor oversight professionals.
  • Build leadership capability and bench strength while creating a culture of accountability, sound judgment, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
  • Set clear goals and expectations and ensure the team has the tools, resources, and direction needed to deliver results.

Drive enterprise partnership and improvement

  • Partner with Legal, Compliance, Finance, Actuarial, Underwriting, Procurement, Operations, Technology, and business leaders on contracts, controls, data, reporting, systems, and service delivery.
  • Develop and present performance dashboards, trend analysis, risk assessments, and strategic recommendations to senior and executive leadership.
  • Lead continuous improvement initiatives across TPA processes, controls, technology, training, and operating models.

Manage financial performance

  • Oversee department expenses as well as TPA fees, loss adjustment expenses, claim payments, reserves, vendor charges, and audit-related costs within delegated authority.
  • Identify leakage and adverse financial trends, validate contractual billing and service outcomes, and drive corrective action.
  • Establish financial performance targets and communicate results, trends, and risks to senior leadership.

What You'll Bring


Required Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • 10+ years of claims or related P&C insurance experience, including experience with TPA, vendor, program, or outsourced claims oversight.
  • 5+ years of progressive leadership experience, including leading managers or multiple teams.
  • Adjuster licenses for applicable states, with the ability to obtain and maintain additional licenses as needed.
  • Deep knowledge of claim investigation, policy interpretation, coverage analysis, reserving, litigation management, settlement practices, fraud indicators, regulatory requirements, and claims financial controls.
  • Demonstrated experience establishing governance models, service levels, vendor performance standards, claims audit programs, and corrective action plans.
  • Experience interpreting and negotiating contracts, statements of work, authority levels, fee structures, reporting obligations, and governance requirements.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence senior internal stakeholders and external business partners and drive accountability without direct authority.
  • Experience managing budgets and using operational and financial data to identify trends, determine root causes, and drive measurable action plans.
  • Strong executive communication, presentation, negotiation, relationship management, and change leadership skills.

We'd Especially Like to See

  • Bachelor's degree in business, insurance, risk management, finance, or a related field.
  • Experience leading multiple TPAs, outsourced claim programs, complex vendor relationships, or multi-state claims operations.
  • Experience with procurement, contract negotiation, vendor risk management, implementations, conversions, or TPA transitions.
  • Professional insurance designation such as AIC, CPCU, or SCLA .
  • Experience with claims analytics, dashboards, quality assurance programs, process improvement, or enterprise change initiatives.
  • Experience presenting to senior and executive leadership and contributing to broader claims strategy.


What Success Looks Like


In this role, success means building a TPA operating model that delivers:

  • Consistent, high-quality claim outcomes
  • Strong regulatory and contractual compliance
  • Improved cycle time and customer experience
  • Appropriate reserves and settlement outcomes
  • Reduced leakage and unnecessary expense
  • Clear accountability across TPA partners
  • Strong visibility into performance, risk, and financial results
  • Continuous improvement in claims controls, technology, and operational effectiveness

Work Environment & Travel


This role operates in a fast-paced, highly regulated environment and involves managing multiple external partners, competing priorities, confidential claim information, and significant financial and operational accountability.

Travel may be required for TPA site visits, business reviews, audits, implementation meetings, and leadership sessions. Occasional schedule flexibility may also be necessary to support urgent claims issues, catastrophe events, regulatory deadlines, or other critical operational needs.


Pay Range

$103,800.00 - $173,300.00
